name: Google Calendar
author: leonavas
description: Google Calendar in the bar: what is on now or next as a label, and a day/week time grid popup you can click through into meetings.

barWidget.description: Next meeting in the bar, with Google Calendar's own day/week grid behind it — click an event to open it, or join the call.

schema.label: Default view
schema.description: Which range the popup opens on. d, 3 and w switch it while it is open.

schema.label: Week view shows Monday to Friday only
schema.description: Drops Saturday and Sunday from the week view, and narrows the popup to match.

schema.label: Week starts on
schema.description: Locale follows the same first day the rest of the desktop uses.

schema.label: Show the ISO week number
schema.description: Printed in the gutter above the hour labels, e.g. W35.

schema.label: Show events you declined
schema.description: Off by default, matching Google Calendar. Shown struck through when on.

schema.label: Height of one hour (px)
schema.description: Taller rows fit event titles more comfortably; shorter ones fit more of the day on screen.

schema.label: Height of the popup's grid (px)
schema.description: How much of the day is visible before it scrolls. Capped by the screen.

schema.label: Hour the grid opens on
schema.description: Used when you are looking at another day. On today it opens an hour before now instead.

schema.label: Days of history to keep
schema.description: How far back the popup can be paged before it runs out of events.

schema.label: Open meeting links as
schema.description: App window runs omarchy-launch-webapp, so the call gets its own window instead of a tab behind the browser.

schema.label: Other Google accounts to offer
schema.description: Comma-separated addresses. The calendar's own account is always offered first; add the others you are signed into so a left click on Join can pick between them. Links are pinned with authuser=<address> rather than /u/<number>/, which shifts as accounts are added or removed.

schema.label: What the bar shows
schema.description: Next event reads "10:00 Standup"; Countdown reads "Standup in 12m".

schema.label: Glyph
schema.description: Any Nerd Font character. Drawn to the left of the label.

schema.label: Longest event title in the bar
schema.description: Longer titles are elided, so one long meeting name cannot push the rest of the bar around.

schema.label: Colour the label this long before an event (minutes)
Remove the widget from the bar when nothing is scheduled
Middle click joins the next meeting
schema.description: Falls back to forcing a sync when the next event has no call attached.

schema.label: Right click on the bar
schema.description: New meeting opens meet.google.com/new as the calendar's own account, so the call is created by the right identity. Syncing is still available from the panel (the refresh button, or r), and runs on its own anyway.

schema.label: Copy the link when starting a new meeting
schema.description: meet.google.com/new is a redirect, so the room only exists once the browser follows it. The code is read back from the browser window title a moment later and the link is put on the clipboard, with a notification. Existing events carry their link already — the card's Copy link button is immediate.

schema.label: Notify when a meeting starts
schema.description: A toast at the moment an event begins; clicking it opens the call, or the event in Google Calendar when there is no call attached. Sent at critical urgency so it waits to be clicked rather than fading. Declined and all-day events are skipped, and meetings that started before the shell did are not replayed.
